_note: D-SETTINGS-LIST-MODELS-HAS-NO-DETAIL-SELECTOR-AND-A-10KB-DEFAULT. The default reply was 10,382 bytes / ~2,595 tokens for 18 models x 15 fields, with no detail selector and no limit. This asks the plainest possible question so the DEFAULT shape is what reaches the model.

scenarios.prompt: Which of my registered models can do tool calling?
scenarios.prompt_source: A plain user question that needs the DEFAULT shape and one of the fields the summary deliberately KEEPS (capability_flags). It does not name the tool, and it does not ask for pricing or timestamps - so if the summary dropped something load-bearing, the answer degrades here rather than in a test I wrote to pass.
scenarios.approve_why: Tier R, user-scoped, no write at any point - this is the read the Context Budget Law exists to protect.
scenarios.falsifier: REFUTED IF: the model cannot name a tool-calling model from the reply (the summary dropped a field the question needs); OR it calls settings_list_models more than twice (the page/limit made it thrash); OR it reaches for detail=full to answer a question the summary should already answer.

ship_audit.absent_case: an account with no models is not covered here.
ship_audit.tenancy: user-scoped by envelope; the tool takes no user argument.

answer_expect.why: Deliberately loose on wording. The real assertion is the TRACE: the call must succeed, and the reply the model summarised must be the small shape.

scenarios._no_seed_assert_why: Nothing is seeded - the tool reads the caller's own registered models, which already exist. A seed here would be inventing substrate for a read that has real substrate.
